**Failure mode** — Connection failure (missing scope on the Gmail Connection).

**Where it went wrong** — Step 2 of the AOP. The Agent correctly read the input and called `gmail.send_message` at transcript turn [2]. The call was rejected at turn [3] because the **Purchasing** Gmail Connection was never granted the send scope. Step 3 (the Google Sheets log) never ran, because the Agent stopped after the send failed. That is correct behaviour, since the AOP only logs a reminder that was sent.

**Evidence**
- Transcript [3]: `ERROR 403: Request had insufficient authentication scopes. Required: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`
- Context: Gmail Connection 'Purchasing' granted scopes: `gmail.readonly, gmail.labels.`

The AOP relies on sending email, but the Connection holds only read and label scopes. The 403 is the symptom. The root cause is the scope mismatch between what Step 2 needs and what the Connection was authorised for. This will fail on every Run until the scope is added, whatever the PO data is.

**Fix** — Extend the **Gmail** Connection 'Purchasing' to include the `gmail.send` scope (https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send). This usually means reconnecting and re-authorising it with the send permission.

**Next step** — Re-authorise the 'Purchasing' Connection with `gmail.send` in Setup, then re-run PO 4500918821. The reminder for that PO (due 2026-10-20) was never sent and nothing was logged to "PO reminders", so it still needs to go out. No AOP rewrite is needed, so there is no `aop-writer` handoff. You could optionally add a failure branch to Step 2 later, but the scope is the actual cause.
